note: Nine §4 hypotheses measured against the Host-S1 parent. Each records its source, baseline behaviour, actual input, observed output, invariant, evidence class and what remains uncertain. A finding marked reproduced describes the PARENT's behaviour; the correction is asserted by the suites named in the corresponding S1R verdict.

findings.title: Rename-before-verify exclusivity: a stale observation moves a newly installed live lock, and the recovery then livelocks
findings.baselineBehavior: Recovery reads the lock's owner, decides it is abandoned, then renames the PATHNAME to a private claim and verifies the token AFTERWARDS. The rename is unconditional on identity, so the object moved may be a successor installed after the observation. The claim name is `active.lock.claim-<ownerToken>`, deterministic per process, and the loop's timeout check is skipped on the abandoned path, so a second pass that collides with its own leftover claim does not terminate.

actualInput.interleaving: a live successor (pid = recoverer process) installed immediately before the recoverer's rename; a third process attempts mkdir immediately after it

findings.invariant: At any instant within the exclusion domain, at most one owner holds execution authority, and a live owner's lock is never moved or deleted by a process acting on a different observation.
findings.additionalDefect: the recovery did not terminate within the bound after colliding with its own claim path
findings.uncertain: The successor here is a synthetic holder record, not a second real host process; what is demonstrated is that the object at the pathname can be replaced between observation and removal, which is the property, not the process identity.

findings.title: Release recovery and unknown ownership
findings.baselineBehavior: Malformed entries are classified before liveness; an unreadable record refuses acquisition and release; release removes only its own token and preserves the rest.

malformedAcquire.detail: the capacity record contains 1 malformed holder entr(y/ies) (pid-not-a-positive-integer), so ownership is UNKNOWN and capacity cannot be gra

unreadablePeek.detail: the capacity record is not valid JSON; capacity is UNKNOWN

releaseResult.detail: the slot was not released: injected ENOSPC

findings.invariant: Unknown ownership never becomes free capacity; a failed read never authorises rewriting an empty holder set; a release removes only the releasing handle's verified record.
defects: a retry after a failed write could not release the handle's own record
findings.uncertain: A genuinely failed record WRITE (as opposed to an unreadable record) is exercised in the capacity suite with an injected filesystem boundary, not here.

findings.title: Cross-repository capacity scope: two ACTIVE worlds in different repositories
findings.baselineBehavior: The slot is keyed by <repository>/.palimpsest/host-capacity/, so two repositories never contend. The design assumes a repository is the confidentiality domain.
findings.invariant: No two Confidential Workers that lack mutual read isolation may simultaneously acquire execution authority; the exclusion scope must match the actual isolation scope.
findings.uncertain: The probe runs under the real DSH ACL sandbox with both worlds granted, which is the measured ACTIVE state; it does not run two full agent sessions concurrently.

findings.title: File-directed links are gated out before reparse classification
findings.baselineBehavior: The walk stats an entry and RETURNS when it is not a directory, so the lstat-based reparse classification below is never reached for a link whose target is a file. A DIRECTORY junction does reach it, so the omission is specific to the file-target class.

actualInput.note: a file symlink is refused (EPERM) here; a junction aimed at a file creates a BROKEN link (statSync ENOENT)

findings.invariant: Every reparse point inside a protected tree is classified by its target, whatever the target's type; a link to content outside the protection domain is never silently counted as covered.
findings.fixtureLimit: a file-directed symlink could not be created on this host (EPERM), so the FILE-link case is SOURCE_DEMONSTRATED rather than dynamically exercised
findings.uncertain: Whether a Low token could READ through a file-directed link is not measurable here, because no such fixture can be created. What is established is that the code would not classify it at all.

findings.title: A declared protected root is treated as a verified protection outcome
findings.baselineBehavior: A link whose target lies under any DECLARED protected root is classified as `reparseIntoProtectedRoot` and excluded from the unresolvable set, so it never makes the walk fail. The declaration is not evidence that the target object carries a verified label.
findings.invariant: A path being inside a DECLARED root is not sufficient; the protection basis must be an actual verified Kernel label on the target.
findings.uncertain: The target here is unlabelled because it was never planned; the same classification would occur if labelling had been attempted and failed, which is the case that matters.

findings.title: An unknown external reparse target receives an unconditional positive qualification
findings.baselineBehavior: A link that RESOLVES but points outside every protected root is recorded as `reparseOutsideProtectionDomain` and leaves `admissionEligible` true. Nothing distinguishes a qualified DSH dependency from an unknown external path or model-controlled content.

actualInput.link: junction -> an arbitrary directory outside every protected root, containing a synthetic canary

findings.invariant: An unknown or mutable target must not receive an unconditional positive qualification; the exception must be a qualified, identified dependency contract.
findings.uncertain: The measured fact that a labelled junction still delivers its target's bytes to a Low token is in junction-label-probe.mjs; this finding is about ADMISSION, not the read.

findings.title: Conformance evidence is loaded from fixed user directories with no run relationship
findings.baselineBehavior: The generator reads `<USERPROFILE>/.palimpsest-r1hr/conformance/conformance.json` and `.palimpsest-r1hc/...` and admits them with `read: true` and a pass count. The receipt carries no Code Freeze HEAD, run id, command, exit code or artifact digest, so a report from any earlier run is admitted identically.

actualInput.content: two passing checks, no run identity

findings.invariant: Current-run conformance must be tied to the Code Freeze and the executed command; a historical report may be used for comparison, never as unqualified current execution evidence.
findings.uncertain: The demonstration replays the loader's admission logic rather than invoking the whole generator; the negative controls in C4 exercise the corrected gate end to end.

findings.title: The final exit code and suite verdicts are not driven by the qualification result
findings.source: scripts/host_s1/generate-evidence.mjs :: runSuite() and the final process.exit()
findings.baselineBehavior: `runSuite` computes PASS from the JSON report alone and ignores the child's exit code; skipped tests are counted but never block PASS; the final `process.exit` depends on producer and suite verdicts only, never on the derived final verdicts.
findings.invariant: RequiredVerdict NOT_ESTABLISHED => nonzero qualification exit; a nonzero child exit, a missing report, zero executed tests or a required skip is never PASS.
findings.uncertain: The negative controls are built and run in C4; this finding records the baseline control flow.

findings.title: A fully enumerated skipped ancestor containing only the active world is refused
findings.source: host/deployment/runtime/read_fence.js :: coverageOf() — `skippedWithoutDerivedCoverage` from an empty derived list
findings.baselineBehavior: `coverageOf` marks any skipped ancestor with no derived roots as `skippedWithoutDerivedCoverage`, so `complete` is false even when the derivation enumerated every level and found nothing but the spine.

actualInput.layout: .palimpsest/worlds/attempt-A, with no sibling worlds and no durable state

findings.invariant: Security failure and overconservative refusal must remain distinguishable: an ancestor that was fully enumerated and genuinely contains only the authorized world is not a confidentiality violation.
findings.uncertain: Whether the refusal is acceptable as a permanent conservative policy is a product decision; §7.5 asks only that it be distinguishable from a security failure.
